signoff.notes: SELL Rp84 (-32%) is the most likely path. At Rp124 the market capitalises a fleet-filled run-rate on two customers at c.46% of revenue with no disclosed contract term [S2], against filed 9M2026 FCFF of -94.6bn and IDR143.6bn of leases ranking ahead of the equity [S0][S2]. Construction follows the house default 60/25/15 with base 45% >= 40% and mirrored +/-10pp growth, +/-2.5pp margin, -/+5pp capex. Target composition is disclosed and acceptable: the DCF leg is floored at nil (EV 110.0bn vs 209.1bn net debt), so the 15% P/E leg (15.7x own history, Rp212) carries the blend and the 20% bull supplies c.60% of the weighted Rp94; the report states this plainly in s4. The inert bear is a disclosed engine floor (s5), not a hidden input; the base case itself is Rp47 (-62%), so the SELL is robust whether the target is read at 47 or 84. No conservatism stack: nwc, tax 24%, capex convention and interest rate are each anchored to the LK/pack with a source. QC second-round items are not material to the call: Q1 (H2 capex inside the floored DCF) cannot lift EV above the 209.1bn net debt even crediting the c.73bn, so the leg stays floored; Q3/Q5 are record-consistency; Q4's COE presentation lifts the target slightly and does not change the rating. Coherent with the desk: the SELL cohort (TAXI, MITI, SAPX) is exactly the names where DCF/FCFF sits below the traded price.

bias.note: Round-1 fixes verified in the files, not the replies: the 85.6bn bridge is gone (valuation.bridge null, DCF deducts the 30-Jun-2026 net debt of 209.14bn = 213.746-4.609, prorated 0.5038 from that date) [S0]; the FY2025A D&A restatement is in the model at 10.4262 = 2 x the H1-2025 fixed-asset charge of 5.2131 [S6], giving FY2025A EBITDA 19.129 on pack EBIT 8.703; the registry check is cited in s6 as [S7] with free float 25.69%, HSC not listed at 11-Nov-2026, no index deletion and no enforcement. Base-case drivers are sourced from the filed 9M2026 (revenue 97.28, gross profit 48.98, opex 27.62) [S2] and the FY2024 LK [S4]; no default haircut is visible in revenue, margin, tax (24% above statutory) or NWC (30% held flat). Two construction defects point opposite ways and roughly offset: the DCF's uniform first-year proration charges H2 with half of FY2026E capex (73.3bn) although the 9M PPE rise of 117.94bn against full-year capex of 146.58 implies H2 additions near zero [S2] - too bearish, about 72bn of EV, worth ~10/share on the bull-weighted target; and the bear case still returns the base value, so 35% of the weight sits on a number the downside cannot move - flattering the target by ~5/share. Neither moves the rating, so neutral.

findings.finding: The DCF's first flow is a uniform 0.5038 of FY2026E FCFF (-47.7bn), so it charges H2-2026 with 73.3bn of the 146.58bn full-year capex, but the report's own balance sheet says the build was done by September: net PPE rose 251.95 -> 369.89 in nine months against 9M D&A of about 29bn, i.e. ~147bn of additions inside the first three quarters [S2], and the model's own H2 path has net debt falling 24.8bn (June actual 209.14 to FY2026E 184.34). The prorated flow and the balance sheet cannot both be right, and s5 asserts 'roughly half of the FY2026E capex' is in the H2 flow. This understates the DCF (floored in base, but the bull unfloors) by roughly 72bn of EV.

The bear is still inert: bear v0/tp are 38.63141260510458 / 46.83817718354274, identical to base, while the bull now differs (231.98 / 281.27). The mirroring is fixed (revenue growth +/-10pp, gross margin -/+2.5pp, capex +5pp in the bear and -5pp in the bull, which are the right signs), but because the earnings legs are struck on pack LTM (EBITDA 28.46, NP 10.62) and the DCF is floored, the contract-loss bear cannot move a single rupiah. A 35% weight on a state that produces no downside is not a probability-weighted value.

The C2 answer still says 'net borrowing 115/30/18/8/0 rolls debt to 195bn in FY2026E and 225bn in FY2027E', but fund record and fund record carry 143.8/30/18/8/0 and debt of 223.79bn / 253.79bn, which is what the report prints (223.8bn) [S0]. The reply is stale against the file it describes.

The judge's note stands on presentation: the stated CAPM inputs (7.4% + 2.30 x (4.2% + 2.5%)) give 22.81%, not the 21.24% used to roll v0 forward to tp_base. It raises the target slightly and does not change the rating.

The judge's FIX is a date confusion and should not be acted on by forcing the line: FY2026E net debt of 184.34bn is the 31-Dec-2026 forecast from the flow model (np+da 49.09 less capex 146.58 and dNWC 9.48 on opening 77.38), while 209.14bn is the 30-Jun-2026 actual deducted by the valuation [S0]. Two dates, not two companies. The defect is the intra-year profile in Q1, not the year-end line.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +25.3pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The step is real and sourced, not a modelling choice. The FY2025A comparative is now restated, not left on the data pack: its EBITDA is 19.13bn (25.9% margin) after restoring the fixed-asset depreciation from the interim LK, because the pack's 6.62bn is the G&A line only - the same line was 7.553bn of a 10.436bn audited total in FY2024 [S6][S4]. FY2026E EBITDA of 68.2bn is a 51.2% margin on a full year of the fleet that was still being added through 2026: nine-month 2026 revenue of 97.28bn against 53.38bn, gross profit 48.98bn, net profit 10.70bn, and net fixed assets of 369.89bn from 251.95bn at end-2025 on 143.56bn of finance leases [S2]. The residual lift over the restated comparative is volume arriving on an asset base bought for it, and the maintenance fade is carried in gross_margin from FY2027E.

flags.message: a.gross_margin moves -4.8pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The 4.8pp fade from 49.6% to 44.8% is the maintenance mechanic, not a caution margin. Truck operating costs, repairs and tyres sat at 52.0bn of a 66.7bn cost base in FY2024 and the charge rises with fleet age [S4]; the 2025-26 additions reach their first heavy maintenance cycle from FY2028, and driver-partner rates reset with the minimum wage. The FY2026E start of 49.6% is the filed nine months at 50.3% blended with the third quarter's 47.7% exit rate, and FY2027E starts at that exit rate, not at the peak [S2].

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -82.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The fall from 110% to 28% is the build-out ending, not a haircut. Net fixed assets rose from 251.95bn to 369.89bn in nine months while depreciation ran, so gross additions ran near 130bn in 2026, funded by 143.56bn of finance leases [S2]. From FY2027 the fleet is in place and capex runs 6pp above the 22% depreciation charge, which is the net investment 4% growth needs on a fleet carried at about 1.5x revenue [S4].

flags.message: nwc FY2025A restated at -0.27x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's -114.9bn is not operating capital. Its FY2025 current liabilities of 216.1bn carry the short-term fleet financing and the current portion of the lease book, which are debt, and the engine then treats a 148bn swing from that negative base as an operating cash inflow in FY2026 [S2]. Restated to receivables 11.96bn plus inventory 23.25bn less payables 4.69bn, operating working capital is 30.5bn; the 23.25bn of inventory is real-estate stock in the property subsidiaries, not unsold trucks [S4].
